A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EquiReg. Their main texts, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–L support reliable comparison, including matching material relocated between versions.

before.justification: v2 reports original image-restoration experiments on FFHQ and ImageNet, PDE reconstruction results, and supplementary empirical analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains original image-restoration and PDE results and reports additional architecture, symmetry, and sampling diagnostics.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 changes the DPS regularization coefficient from λt to ζtλt, coupling it to measurement guidance. The MPE loss and other solver constructions remain substantially unchanged. Appendix E supports the new scaling, but Algorithm 6 retains the unscaled update, leaving the implemented procedure ambiguous.

E1.justification: The principal FFHQ, ImageNet, text-guided generation, Helmholtz, and Navier–Stokes coverage remains. Figures 17–18 and 21 add limited test scenarios involving mixtures with Gaussian/uniform white noise and lattice versus off-lattice translations.

E2.justification: The diversity comparison removes DPS from all three tasks: v2 Table 7 contains DPS and Equi-DPS, whereas v3 Table 6 contains only Equi-DPS. The main restoration and PDE comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix E replaces the stated final-10% regularization shutdown for unscaled experiments with constant λt throughout all experiments and describes effective DPS scaling by ζt. New diagnostics introduce controlled architecture comparisons and a joint λ/ζ sweep. These are reported setting changes; the PDFs do not establish whether retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Figures 17–22 substantially expand mechanism and robustness analysis through architecture controls, translation equivariance, trajectory drift, likelihood error, white noise, and joint guidance-strength sensitivity. Conversely, v2's DPS reduced-DDIM-step analysis and ImageNet qualitative comparison are removed, and the diversity analysis loses its baseline rows.

E5.justification: New Figure 20 reports paired means with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals and paired sign-test significance at p<0.05. These statistical procedures were absent from v2. The existing fixed-seed comparisons and 20-image, 10-seed diversity design remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 3b revises DPS substantially: super-resolution FID changes from 125.4 to 65.15 while Equi-DPS remains 51.00, shrinking the reported advantage. The MPE comparison changes ImageNet baseline SSIM from 0.407 to 0.612, reversing its comparison with unchanged regularized values of 0.568. Diagnostic results are added, while DPS diversity rows, MPE-table FID values, and reduced-step results are removed.

T1.justification: v3 removes Proposition G.2, the reweighted functional, and Appendix G.4's derivation connecting regularized sampling to an approximate Wasserstein flow. Proposition G.1 and its proof for ideal conditional dynamics remain. The manifold-constrained definition is retained as Definition H.2, relocated from Definition 3.2.

C1.justification: The introduction narrows its diversity framing from favorable fidelity–diversity tradeoffs to improved fidelity without posterior collapse. The central claims about MPE regularization, broad applicability, reconstruction improvement, and acceleration remain substantially unchanged.

C2.justification: The approximate reweighted-flow explanation is withdrawn in favor of a motivational Wasserstein perspective. v3 adds substantive explanations involving training-distribution match, architectural bias, and measurement-guidance strength. It also distinguishes pointwise equivariance from distributional invariance and explicitly acknowledges that diversity diagnostics do not establish posterior calibration.

D1.justification: v3 replaces the promised post-acceptance code release with a public repository link. It more explicitly identifies the encoder versus decoder used by each solver, reuse of pretrained autoencoders, group selection, and regularization scaling. Most implementation tables and hardware information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 expands distinctions from existing cited approaches, including Terris et al.'s denoiser symmetrization, Hoogeboom et al.'s architectural equivariance, and Daras et al.'s temporal consistency. The Zheng et al. (2025) Ensemble Kalman Diffusion Guidance reference is removed.

P1.justification: The revision makes localized prose refinements and expands explanations while retaining the overall section structure. It moves the EquiCon definition to Appendix H and the detailed DreamSampler discussion to Appendix A, and updates publication information, affiliations, and acknowledgements.

P2.justification: Six diagnostic figures are added, several older figures are removed, and numerous displays are relocated or reformatted. The characterization table moves from main-text Table 1 to Appendix Table 13 with reduced content; the diversity table loses comparator rows and the MPE table loses its FID column. Several captions and schematic labels are expanded.

improvement.justification: v3 adds useful diagnostics, statistical reporting, clearer theoretical limits, and code-access information. However, it removes comparative evidence and introduces unresolved inconsistencies: Algorithms 1 and 6 disagree on DPS scaling, and the retained 59% FID-improvement claim conflicts with updated Table 3 values implying about 22%. Appendix D also retains comparative conclusions after removing DPS rows. The sparsely documented new diagnostics and these losses prevent a reliable net-quality judgment.
